column1: # Gaming. Included only when $PROFILE is desktop; --no-gaming opts out.
# NB: "desktop" here means the desktop MACHINE. packages/desktop.tsv is a
# different thing entirely - it means the graphical session and is installed on
# both machines. The collision is unfortunate and predates this file.
# NB: multilib must be enabled for any of the lib32-* rows to resolve. CachyOS
# enables it by default; doctor.sh checks the live repo list rather than
# trusting pacman.conf, because a missing multilib presents as "steam: command
# not found" long after the bootstrap that skipped it.

column5: from multilib. NB: keep game libraries on the NVMe - Steam does not support NTFS libraries and Proton breaks on its case-insensitivity and lack of symlinks, so the 1 TB storage disk is the wrong place for them
udev rules for controllers; without it a gamepad is visible to root only

Valve's micro-compositor. On an RX 570 the real lever is rendering at 720p and letting gamescope upscale to the 1080p panel (-w 1280 -h 720 -W 1920 -H 1080 -F fsr)
non-Steam game manager; also the least painful way to drive a Wine prefix by hand

Epic Games, GOG and Amazon libraries. This is the Epic Games Launcher replacement: it wraps `legendary`, the CLI Epic client, in a GUI that installs and launches through Proton/Wine. legendary alone is command-line only. NB: put its game library on the same disk as Steam's, not in $HOME - see docs/DESKTOP.md
stock Wine, for Lutris prefixes and anything Proton does not cover. NB: it is NOT here for Affinity any more - that was dropped; see packages/creative.tsv
.NET for Wine. Plenty of Windows game launchers and installers are .NET, and without it they fail with a Mono download prompt that goes nowhere offline
